**Summary**

**EuroCOMP Lab evaluations**

## Spain: Financial support to innovate

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
**The problem**

Market failures keep research and development (R&D) investment in Extremadura below
its optimal level. Small and medium firms in the region under-invest in innovation,
particularly in agriculture and the ecological transition.
:::
::: {.card-e}
**What was done**

The Regional Government of Extremadura (JUNTA) and the Extremadura Science and
Technology Park Foundation (FUNDECYT-PCTEx) created an EU-funded matching grant
programme for small and medium firms.

Each cycle awards €3.5 million in grants, up to €250,000 per firm (€138,000 on
average), financing 35% to 80% of a firm's proposed R&D investment.
:::
:::

### What experimentation sought to answer

::: {.quote-e}
"What is the impact of R&D grants on SMEs' business performance?"
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Lottery</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Program</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Impact</span></div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="facts">
  <div><div class="k">The programme</div><div class="v">Matching grants of up to EUR 250,000 per firm (average EUR 138,000) for R&D projects</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="v">Extremadura, Spain; regional government (JUNTA) with FUNDECYT-PCTEx, EU-funded</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Who is randomized</div><div class="v">Firms: SME applicants, mainly agriculture and ecological transition, scored on 11 criteria</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">The design</div><div class="v">Bin-ranking RCT: the middle bin randomized, 22 funded vs. 34 not funded</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Outcomes tracked</div><div class="v">Private R&D investment, implementation success, expected sales growth</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Starting point</div><div class="v">Market failures keep regional R&D investment below its optimal level</div></div>
</div>
```

### From application to evidence

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Applications</div>
  <div>External scoring</div>
  <div>Middle-bin lottery</div>
  <div>R&D grants</div>
  <div>Follow-up survey</div>
</div>
```


### How the programme was tested

Extremadura ran an advertising campaign to attract at least 100 applicants. External
reviewers scored every application on 11 objective criteria and grouped proposals into
low, medium and high quality.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
<svg viewBox="0 0 660 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Applications scored on 11 criteria; high scorers funded automatically, low scorers rejected automatically, and only the medium-quality middle band of 56 firms is randomized into 22 funded and 34 not funded">
  <text x="20" y="24" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold">Quality score</text>

  <rect x="90" y="34" width="280" height="56" rx="5" fill="#F2C94C"/>
  <text x="230" y="58" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">High quality</text>
  <text x="230" y="76" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="11">accepted and funded automatically</text>

  <rect x="90" y="100" width="280" height="96" rx="5" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#F2C94C" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="230" y="126" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Medium quality: 56 firms</text>
  <text x="230" y="145" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11">equally eligible, randomized by lottery</text>
  <text x="230" y="163" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11">22 funded &middot; 34 not funded</text>
  <text x="230" y="181" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11">this band is the sample for study</text>

  <rect x="90" y="206" width="280" height="52" rx="5" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="230" y="230" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Low quality</text>
  <text x="230" y="248" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11">rejected automatically</text>

  <path d="M382 148 H410" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <rect x="410" y="116" width="230" height="64" rx="5" fill="rgba(242,201,76,.16)"/>
  <text x="425" y="138" fill="#2B2724" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold">Only the middle band is randomized</text>
  <text x="425" y="156" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11">The strongest and weakest applicants</text>
  <text x="425" y="170" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11">are handled by the score, not the draw</text>

  <text x="20" y="290" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11.5">This design works well when eligibility criteria are clear and resources are limited.</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Extremadura's bin-ranking design: only medium-quality applicants, the band where expected returns are least certain, are randomized.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

::: {.soft-panel}
**Why this design.** Strength: it leverages investment-return uncertainty for
applications with unclear returns. Limitation: it requires a large sample size in the
middle range (bin).
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Randomisation successfully balanced key firm characteristics: the comparison group and
the treatment group looked the same on average. There was no evidence of firms with
certain characteristics dropping out of the study more than others (selective
attrition) in follow-up survey responses.
:::

### What the programme achieved

Three months after receiving the grant, firms in the treatment group reported higher
planned R&D investment and stronger confidence in their projects than the comparison
group.

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
[+48%]{.num}

**More planned R&D investment for 2025**

€65,000 above the comparison-group average.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[67%]{.num}

**Probability of successful implementation**

Up from 16% without funding, according to expert priors.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[×2]{.num}

**Expected sales growth, conditional on success**

From 8% to 16% after receiving the grant, according to expert priors.
:::
:::

::: {.caution}
Over half of the comparison-group firms planned to continue their R&D projects using
other funding or their own resources. Public R&D subsidies can significantly boost
private investment, but careful targeting is needed to avoid simply displacing money
firms would have spent anyway.
:::

## Czechia: light-touch support for SMEs

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
**The problem**

Entrepreneurial activity remains low in Czech regions hit by the decline of the coal
industry. These regions need to diversify away from carbon-intensive industries and
grow their private sector.

In September 2022, the European Commission approved the Just Transition Programme
(JTP): €1.641 billion for business R&D, post-mining regeneration, skills, clean energy
and the circular economy in the Moravian-Silesian, Ústí and Karlovy Vary regions.

A key part of the JTP is a voucher scheme for entrepreneurs: up to €21,100 for business
development, up to €42,200 for innovation, and up to €21,100 for digital transformation.
:::
::: {.card-e}
**What was done**

The World Bank tested two light-touch, complementary pilots that add skills support on
top of the voucher scheme.

**Smart Start** (Moravian-Silesian region): seven workshops teaching a scientific
approach to decision-making under uncertainty, covering risk versus uncertainty,
hypothesis testing and A/B testing, aimed at voucher recipients and other interested
firms.

**AI Klub** (Ústí and Karlovy Vary regions): five hands-on workshops on using AI for
efficiency, marketing, sales, product development and financial management, with
peer-to-peer exchange between firms.
:::
:::

### What experimentation sought to answer

::: {.quote-e}
"Does light-touch support to SMEs improve firm capabilities and performance?"
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Lottery</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Program</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Impact</span></div>
```

### Smart Start entrepreneur training

```{=html}
<div class="facts">
  <div><div class="k">The programme</div><div class="v">Smart Start: seven workshops on scientific decision-making and customer validation</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="v">Ostrava, Moravian-Silesian region; Just Transition Programme with MSIC</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Who is randomized</div><div class="v">246 interested firms, many of them entrepreneurial voucher applicants</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">The design</div><div class="v">Simple lottery with unequal shares: 163 invited to the training vs. 83 with no support</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Outcomes tracked</div><div class="v">Business changes, motivations for change, sales and firm performance</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Starting point</div><div class="v">Entrepreneurial activity remains low in regions hit by the coal industry's decline</div></div>
</div>
```

### From application to evidence

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Interest sign-up</div>
  <div>Random selection</div>
  <div>Seven workshops</div>
  <div>Presentations</div>
  <div>Follow-up survey</div>
</div>
```

### AI adoption in post-coal regions

```{=html}
<div class="facts">
  <div><div class="k">The programme</div><div class="v">AI Klub: five hands-on workshops on AI for efficiency, marketing, sales, and finance</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="v">Ústí and Karlovy Vary regions; Just Transition Programme with local partners</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Who is randomized</div><div class="v">173 interested firms, including innovation voucher recipients</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">The design</div><div class="v">Simple lottery with unequal shares: 117 invited to the workshops vs. 56 with no support</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Outcomes tracked</div><div class="v">AI adoption and use, innovation, business networking, sales and profits</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Starting point</div><div class="v">Local economies still rely on carbon-intensive industries and need diversification</div></div>
</div>
```

### From application to evidence

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Interest sign-up</div>
  <div>Random selection</div>
  <div>Five AI workshops</div>
  <div>Peer exchange</div>
  <div>Follow-up survey</div>
</div>
```


### How the two pilots were tested

Both pilots drew their sample from firms that had already shown interest, then invited
roughly two in three of them by random selection, leaving the rest as a comparison
group.

### Smart Start &middot; Moravian-Silesian region

  <rect x="210" y="46" width="160" height="66" rx="6" fill="#F2C94C"/>

::: {.col-e}
::: {.col-head}
Smart Start

:::

::: {.col-head}

:::
:::

## Croatia: matching businesses with scientists

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
**The problem**

Firms and scientists in Croatia struggle to collaborate: information frictions,
uncertain transaction costs and limited outreach budgets get in the way, especially for
small and medium firms.

Only 8% of Croatian firms collaborate with higher education institutions, far below the
EU average. A World Bank survey found that 47% of firms lacked information about
relevant scientists.
:::
::: {.card-e}
**What was done**

The World Bank, the Innovation Centre Nikola Tesla and the Ministry of Science,
Education and Youth designed "Scinergy", a business-science matchmaking pilot
targeting fields such as AI, energy and biotechnology.

Matched firms and scientists took part in a two-day matchmaking event in February 2024:
"speed-dating" sessions followed by joint workshops, plus legal and communication
support to help pairs plan R&D projects together.
:::
:::

### What experimentation sought to answer

::: {.quote-e}
"Does connecting firms with scientists foster research partnerships and innovation?"
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Lottery</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Program</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Impact</span></div>
```

### The programme

```{=html}
<div class="facts">
  <div><div class="k">The programme</div><div class="v">Scinergy: matchmaking events, workshops, and ongoing support for firm-scientist pairs</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="v">Croatia; Innovation Centre Nikola Tesla with the Ministry of Science, Education, and Youth</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Who is randomized</div><div class="v">210 eligible firms, from over 250 applications, seeking scientific collaboration</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">The design</div><div class="v">Simple lottery: 100 firms invited to Scinergy vs. 110 not invited</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Outcomes tracked</div><div class="v">Collaboration attempts and partnerships, innovation, R&D employment</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Starting point</div><div class="v">Only 8% of Croatian firms collaborate with higher education, far below the EU average</div></div>
</div>
```

### From application to evidence

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Applications</div>
  <div>Lottery</div>
  <div>Matchmaking event</div>
  <div>Joint R&D planning</div>
  <div>Follow-up survey</div>
</div>
```


### How the programme was tested

Firms applied between November 2023 and January 2024. In February 2024, eligible firms
were randomly assigned by lottery to receive matchmaking support or not.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
<svg viewBox="0 0 700 200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="260 applications are screened down to 210 eligible firms, which enter a lottery splitting them into 100 firms invited to Scinergy and 110 not invited">
  <rect x="10" y="66" width="130" height="66" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="75" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="19" font-weight="bold">260</text>
  <text x="75" y="114" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="10.5">applications</text>

  <path d="M140 99 H166" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <rect x="166" y="66" width="130" height="66" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="231" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="19" font-weight="bold">210</text>
  <text x="231" y="114" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="10.5">eligible firms</text>

  <path d="M296 99 H326" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <rect x="326" y="66" width="130" height="66" rx="6" fill="#F2C94C"/>
  <text x="391" y="92" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">LOTTERY</text>
  <text x="391" y="110" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="10.5">every firm, the same chance</text>

  <path d="M456 99 H486 V34 H516" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <path d="M456 99 H486 V164 H516" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>

  <rect x="516" y="10" width="180" height="48" rx="6" fill="#F2C94C"/>
  <text x="530" y="30" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">100 invited</text>
  <text x="530" y="47" fill="#2B2724" font-size="11">matched with scientists</text>

  <rect x="516" y="140" width="180" height="48" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="530" y="160" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">110 not invited</text>
  <text x="530" y="177" fill="#6B6455" font-size="11">comparison group</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Only firms that cleared eligibility screening entered the lottery, so the comparison group is drawn from the same pool as the firms invited to Scinergy.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

::: {.soft-panel}
**Why this design.** Strength: a lottery among applicants ensures wide outreach,
thanks to a simple application process. Limitation: firms may drop out after applying,
which can reduce statistical power.
:::

### What the programme achieved

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
[+38%]{.num}

**Collaboration attempts with scientists**

Treated firms were more likely to attempt and to sustain collaborations with Croatian
researchers.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[+50%]{.num}

**Commercialisation of new products**

Among firms that originally requested support in AI, who benefited the most from the
pilot.
:::
:::

## Earlier work by the EuroCOMP Lab team: Digitrans 

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
**The problem**

Small businesses in Bulgaria, Poland and Slovakia show limited adoption of digital
tools beyond what regulation or the financial sector requires. The 2022 Digital Economy
and Society Index places all three countries in the bottom quartile of EU members for
business digitalisation.

Current public support programmes in the region largely overlook this: MSMEs account
for 98% of businesses and two-thirds of employment, yet most programmes still emphasise
technology adoption and financial assistance, leaving the managerial and organisational
capabilities firms need to make use of new tools unaddressed.
:::
::: {.card-e}
**What was done**

The World Bank designed Digitrans, a standardised support instrument tested across
Bulgaria, Poland and Slovakia, integrating a financial subsidy with technical
assistance to address both resource and capability constraints.

The financial subsidy provides up to €2,000 per firm towards the cost of adopting
digital business tools. The technical assistance component adds a 10-week programme of
diagnostic assessment, group training and one-to-one advisory support.
:::
:::

### What experimentation sought to answer

::: {.quote-e}
"Does pairing technical assistance with a financial subsidy improve MSME
digitalisation outcomes more than a subsidy alone?"
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Lottery</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Program</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Impact</span></div>
```

### The programme

```{=html}
<div class="facts">
  <div><div class="k">The programme</div><div class="v">A financial subsidy of up to EUR 2,000 per firm, with a subset of firms also receiving a 10-week technical assistance programme</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="v">Bulgaria, Poland and Slovakia; World Bank Digitrans pilot, EU-funded</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Who is randomized</div><div class="v">629 MSMEs with 5&ndash;35 employees and at least 12 months trading, drawn from over 1,600 applications</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">The design</div><div class="v">Three-arm RCT, stratified by country, firm size and digital sophistication: comparison (209), subsidy only (210), subsidy plus technical assistance (210)</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Outcomes tracked</div><div class="v">Digital tool adoption and usage, managerial and organisational change, firm performance</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Starting point</div><div class="v">Small businesses show limited digital adoption beyond what regulation or banks require</div></div>
</div>
```

### From application to evidence

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Applications</div>
  <div>Eligibility & interview</div>
  <div>Random assignment</div>
  <div>Subsidy & support</div>
  <div>Follow-up survey</div>
</div>
```


### How the programme was tested

Firms applied through an open call across Bulgaria, Poland and Slovakia in 2024, and
those meeting the eligibility criteria completed a baseline interview. Eligible firms
were then randomly assigned by the World Bank into one of three groups, with
randomisation stratified within each country by firm size and digital sophistication so
that groups were balanced from the outset.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
<svg viewBox="0 0 700 270" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="629 randomised firms enter a stratified lottery, splitting them into a comparison group of 209 firms, a financial subsidy only group of 210 firms, and a financial subsidy plus technical assistance group of 210 firms">
  <rect x="10" y="90" width="150" height="70" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="85" y="120" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="19" font-weight="bold">629</text>
  <text x="85" y="139" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="10.5">randomised firms</text>

  <path d="M160 125 H196" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <rect x="196" y="90" width="180" height="70" rx="6" fill="#F2C94C"/>
  <text x="286" y="118" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">STRATIFIED LOTTERY</text>
  <text x="286" y="136" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="10.5">by country, size and digital sophistication</text>

  <path d="M376 125 H406" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <path d="M406 125 V28 H436" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <path d="M406 125 H436" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <path d="M406 125 V222 H436" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>

  <rect x="436" y="0" width="254" height="56" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="450" y="22" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">209 comparison group</text>
  <text x="450" y="39" fill="#6B6455" font-size="10.5">benchmarking report only</text>

  <rect x="436" y="97" width="254" height="56" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="450" y="119" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">210 financial subsidy</text>
  <text x="450" y="136" fill="#6B6455" font-size="10.5">subsidy plus benchmarking report</text>

  <rect x="436" y="194" width="254" height="56" rx="6" fill="#F2C94C"/>
  <text x="450" y="216" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">210 subsidy + technical assistance</text>
  <text x="450" y="233" fill="#2B2724" font-size="10.5">the full support package</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Randomisation was stratified within each country by firm size and digital sophistication, splitting 629 eligible firms into a comparison group and two support groups of about 210 firms each.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

::: {.soft-panel}
**Why this design.** Strength: a three-arm design separates the effect of money from
the effect of capability-building support, rather than only comparing supported firms
to unsupported ones. Limitation: it needs a larger sample than a simple two-arm trial to
detect the same effect size, since firms are split three ways.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Allocation resulted in balanced groups across a broad range of firm characteristics,
creating a solid foundation for rigorous impact evaluation. There was no evidence of
systematic differences between groups at baseline, so later changes can be reliably
attributed to the support received rather than to pre-existing differences.
:::

### What the programme achieved

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
[2.5x]{.num}

**Digital tool usage is 2.5x higher with combined support**

Firms that received both types of support increased their digital tool usage intensity
more than twice as much as those with a subsidy alone.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[2x]{.num}

**Managerial changes are more common with technical assistance**

Firms in the combined support group were twice as likely to introduce internal
organisational and managerial changes.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[82% vs 67%]{.num}

**Combined support leads to deeper use of digital tools**

Firms with technical assistance made better use of advanced software functions: 82%
used CRM systems for client communication, against 67% in the subsidy-only group.
:::
:::

::: {.caution}
Firms receiving only a financial subsidy typically limited their spending to the
subsidy value, with no meaningful increase in the sophistication of tools available to
them. Effective digitalisation support needs to go beyond subsidising technology
purchases: the benefits of combined support were especially strong among smaller firms,
firms with low initial digital capabilities, service-sector firms and women-led
businesses.
:::

---

## Examples from beyond the Lab
### Colombia: Scaling up management consulting

Source: [Iacovone, L., Maloney, W. F., & McKenzie, D. (2022). Improving management
with individual and group-based consulting: Results from a randomized experiment in
Colombia. *Review of Economic Studies*, 89(1),
346–371.](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/198461559921937913)

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
**The problem**

Colombian auto parts manufacturers show wide variation in management practices, and
weaker practices are closely tied to lower productivity. Structured, hands-on
management consulting can improve how firms are run, but delivering it in a
resource-intensive, one-on-one format is costly — a cost that can be prohibitive for
small and medium firms to finance on their own, and for governments seeking to support
large numbers of firms at once.
:::
::: {.card-e}
**What was done**

The World Bank, in partnership with the Government of Colombia, tested two lower-cost
ways to deliver management consulting to small and medium manufacturers: individual,
firm-by-firm consulting delivered by local teams, and a more novel group-based model
that works with several firms together to bring costs down further.

Every participating firm, including the comparison group, first received a diagnostic
assessment of its management practices across five areas — logistics, human resources,
finance, marketing and sales, and production — carried out by a team of specialist
consultants.
:::
:::

### What experimentation sought to answer

::: {.quote-e}
"Can lower-cost individual or group-based consulting improve small and medium firms'
management practices and performance?"
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Lottery</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Program</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Impact</span></div>
```

### The programme

```{=html}
<div class="facts">
  <div><div class="k">The programme</div><div class="v">A diagnostic for every firm, followed by individual or group-based management consulting</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="v">Colombia &mdash; auto parts manufacturing sector</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Who is randomized</div><div class="v">159 eligible firms (manufacturers, tier 1/2 suppliers, 2+ years old, 10+ workers), in 53 matched triplets</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">The design</div><div class="v">Three-arm RCT: comparison, individual consulting (~US$28,950/firm), group consulting (~US$10,500/firm)</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Outcomes tracked</div><div class="v">Management practices; employment, sales, value-added and profits via administrative records</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Starting point</div><div class="v">Baseline management scores ranged from 43 to 51 out of 100 across practice areas</div></div>
</div>
```

### From application to evidence

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Applications</div>
  <div>Diagnostic phase</div>
  <div>Matched-triplet lottery</div>
  <div>Consulting delivered</div>
  <div>Outcome tracking</div>
</div>
```


### How the programme was tested

218 firms applied to Colombia's Programa de Extensionismo Tecnológico. After screening
for eligibility — established auto parts manufacturers that were tier 1 or 2 suppliers,
at least two years old, with at least ten employees, and located in Antioquia,
Cundinamarca, Valle del Cauca or the Eje Cafetero — 159 firms formed the final sample.

Firms were then grouped into 53 matched triplets, formed to minimise differences in
location, size, labor productivity and management practices between the three firms in
each triplet. Within each triplet, firms were randomly allocated to a comparison group,
individual consulting, or group consulting.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
<svg viewBox="0 0 700 270" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="159 eligible firms are grouped into 53 matched triplets, balanced on location, size, productivity and management practices; each triplet is then randomly split into a comparison group of 53 firms, an individual consulting group of 53 firms, and a group consulting group of 53 firms">
  <rect x="10" y="90" width="150" height="70" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="85" y="120" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="19" font-weight="bold">159</text>
  <text x="85" y="139" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="10.5">eligible firms</text>

  <path d="M160 125 H196" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <rect x="196" y="90" width="180" height="70" rx="6" fill="#F2C94C"/>
  <text x="286" y="118" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">53 MATCHED TRIPLETS</text>
  <text x="286" y="136" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="10.5">by location, size, productivity, practices</text>

  <path d="M376 125 H406" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <path d="M406 125 V28 H436" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <path d="M406 125 H436" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <path d="M406 125 V222 H436" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>

  <rect x="436" y="0" width="254" height="56" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="450" y="22" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">53 comparison group</text>
  <text x="450" y="39" fill="#6B6455" font-size="10.5">diagnostic only, no consulting</text>

  <rect x="436" y="97" width="254" height="56" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="450" y="119" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">53 individual consulting</text>
  <text x="450" y="136" fill="#6B6455" font-size="10.5">~US$28,950/firm, over 6 months</text>

  <rect x="436" y="194" width="254" height="56" rx="6" fill="#F2C94C"/>
  <text x="450" y="216" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">53 group consulting</text>
  <text x="450" y="233" fill="#2B2724" font-size="10.5">~US$10,500/firm, in groups of 3&ndash;8</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Firms were matched into triplets before randomisation, then randomly allocated within each triplet to a comparison group, individual consulting, or group consulting.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

::: {.soft-panel}
**Why this design.** Strength: matching firms into triplets before randomising keeps
the three groups closely balanced on size, productivity and starting management
practices, even with a modest overall sample. Limitation: with only 53 firms in each
arm, the design has less statistical power to detect small effects than a larger,
simple two-arm trial.
:::

### What the programme achieved

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
[+9 pp]{.num}

**Management practices improved in both groups**

Individual and group consulting each raised firms' management practice scores by
around 9 percentage points on average, relative to a baseline of 56%.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[+28% to +33%]{.num}

**Sales and profits rose for group-consulting firms**

Firms receiving group-based consulting saw significant gains in sales, value-added and
profits; the individual programme's effects on firm performance were smaller and not
statistically significant.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[US$273,000]{.num}

**Estimated average annual profit increase, group consulting**

At a cost of about US$10,500 per firm, the estimated profit gains from group
consulting paid back the programme's cost within about a month.
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Group-consulting firms reported far more contact with each other after the programme
than before it: business links between study firms were almost non-existent at
baseline, but around half of group participants said they still communicated with
other group members roughly a year later, and firms whose management practices changed
the most tended to be grouped with others who also improved the most — evidence that
peer learning, not just lower delivery cost, contributed to the group programme's
stronger results on firm performance.
:::

::: {.caution}
The group programme's rollout was delayed by more than a year due to a budgetary
payment delay, and only 68% of group-assigned firms completed the intervention,
compared with 87% for the individually delivered programme. Delays like this are a
practical risk to weigh when comparing the cost-effectiveness of different delivery
models.
:::

### Yemen: Testing whether internships help youth find work

Source: [McKenzie, D., Assaf, N., & Cusolito, A. P. (2016). The demand for, and
impact of, youth internships: Evidence from a randomized experiment in Yemen. *IZA
Journal of Labor & Development*,
5(1), 1–15.](https://izajold.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s40175-016-0048-8)

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
**The problem**

Young jobseekers in Yemen often face a catch-22: firms are reluctant to hire
someone without prior work experience, yet that experience is hard to gain
without first being hired. Early jobs matter because they build both
job-specific and soft skills, but firms may under-invest in providing them —
a reluctance that can be sharper still in a fragile, conflict-affected
setting. Job opportunities for young graduates were also increasingly scarce
following Yemen's 2011–12 political crisis.
:::
::: {.card-e}
**What was done**

The Enterprise Revitalization and Employment Pilot (EREP) tested a
subsidised-internship model: the program paid half the cost of a six-month
internship, with the host firm covering the rest, and matched applicants to
firms based on the firm's stated requirements. Recent graduates in Sanaa and
Aden applied online and were screened for eligibility before being
considered.
:::
:::

### What experimentation sought to answer

::: {.quote-e}
"Can a subsidised matchmaking program help young jobseekers gain their first
work experience, and does that experience translate into better employment
outcomes afterward?"
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Application</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Random assignment</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Matchmaking</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Impact</span></div>
```

### The programme

```{=html}
<div class="facts">
  <div><div class="k">The programme</div><div class="v">Enterprise Revitalization and Employment Pilot (EREP), internship component &mdash; matching grants covering half the cost of a six-month internship, plus matchmaking between graduates and firms</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="v">Republic of Yemen &mdash; Sanaa and Aden</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Who is randomized</div><div class="v">583 eligible youth (Yemeni, Sanaa/Aden residents, graduated within 2 years), to treatment (430) or control (153)</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">The design</div><div class="v">RCT; treatment group offered matchmaking to internships subsidised at 50% of cost, for up to six months</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Outcomes tracked</div><div class="v">Employment, months worked and earnings, via a follow-up phone survey</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Starting point</div><div class="v">3,487 eligible youth applied; 500 were randomly invited to a two-day basic skills training (477 attended)</div></div>
</div>
```

### From application to evidence

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Applications</div>
  <div>Skills-training invitation</div>
  <div>Random assignment</div>
  <div>Matchmaking</div>
  <div>Follow-up survey</div>
</div>
```


### How the programme was tested

The program launched in August 2013 through a project website, media events and
campus outreach. Applications ran from October to December 2013, closing with
3,487 eligible applicants. Of these, 500 were randomly invited to a two-day
basic skills training — chosen with probability proportional to the demand
for their specialisation — and 477 attended.

The resulting experimental sample of 583 individuals was randomly assigned,
within strata defined by specialisation and city, to a treatment group of 430
(offered matchmaking to a subsidised internship) or a control group of 153.
Eleven human resource advisors then matched treatment-group applicants to
firms based on the firm's requirements, sending CVs for firms to interview
and decide whether to offer a placement.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
<svg viewBox="0 0 760 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="3,487 eligible applicants; 500 are randomly invited to basic skills training and 477 attend; from these, 583 form the experimental sample, randomly assigned within strata to a treatment group of 430 offered internship matchmaking, or a control group of 153">
  <rect x="10" y="95" width="140" height="70" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="80" y="125" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">3,487</text>
  <text x="80" y="144" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="9.5">eligible applicants</text>

  <path d="M150 130 H182" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <rect x="182" y="95" width="160" height="70" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="262" y="120" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">500 invited to training</text>
  <text x="262" y="138" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B6455" font-size="9.5">477 attended</text>

  <path d="M342 130 H374" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <rect x="374" y="95" width="170" height="70" rx="6" fill="#F2C94C"/>
  <text x="459" y="120" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">583 experimental sample</text>
  <text x="459" y="138" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2B2724" font-size="9.5">assigned within 39 strata</text>

  <path d="M544 130 H576" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <path d="M576 130 V48 H606" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <path d="M576 130 V212 H606" stroke="#B9AF95" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>

  <rect x="606" y="20" width="150" height="56" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="620" y="42" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">430 treatment</text>
  <text x="620" y="59" fill="#6B6455" font-size="9.5">offered matchmaking</text>

  <rect x="606" y="184" width="150" height="56" rx="6" fill="#FFFDF7" stroke="#E4DCC6"/>
  <text x="620" y="206" fill="#2B2724" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">153 control</text>
  <text x="620" y="223" fill="#6B6455" font-size="9.5">no internship match</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Applicants were randomly invited to basic skills training, then the resulting sample was randomly assigned, within specialisation-and-city strata, to a treatment group offered internship matchmaking or a control group.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

::: {.soft-panel}
**Why this design.** Strength: randomising within strata defined by
specialisation and city, among applicants who had already been invited to
training, helps ensure the treatment and control groups started out
comparable in skills and local job-market conditions. Limitation: more
applicants were assigned to treatment than there were internship placements
available, so actual take-up (36.7%) fell well below the treatment
assignment rate — which is why the study reports both an intention-to-treat
effect and a larger effect scaled up for those who actually took up an
internship.
:::

### What the programme achieved

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
[+17 pp / +42 pp]{.num}

**More likely to have worked at all in 2014**

Being offered internship matchmaking raised the chance of having worked at
all during 2014 by 17 percentage points on an intention-to-treat basis, and
by 42 percentage points among those who actually took up an internship,
relative to a 61% employment rate in the control group.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[+0.35 s.d. / +0.85 s.d.]{.num}

**Employment gains persisted months after the internship ended**

On a standardised index of employment outcomes measured three to five months
after internships ended, effects remained statistically significant — 0.35
standard deviations on an intention-to-treat basis, and 0.85 standard
deviations for those who took up an internship.
:::
::: {.card-e}
[36.7%]{.num}

**Take-up among those assigned to treatment**

Only 158 of the 430 people assigned to treatment were actually matched to and
completed an internship placement, reflecting how binding capacity
constraints were relative to demand for internship positions.
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
The internship raised employment more for male applicants than for female
applicants, so the program did not close the pre-existing gender gap in
employment outcomes. Because the evaluation covers only one year of the
program rather than the two originally planned, the study had limited
statistical power to say precisely how much smaller the effect was for
women.
:::

::: {.caution}
Conflict escalated partway through the program: Houthi forces took control of
Sanaa in September 2014, and the second year of the pilot was cancelled,
roughly halving the intended sample and reducing statistical power. The
follow-up survey was also fielded earlier and more narrowly than planned,
amid displacement and shortages of fuel, electricity and water. It also
remains possible that some of the employment gains for treated youth came
partly at the expense of other jobseekers in the economy — a general
equilibrium effect this study could not measure.
:::
